question: A clinical operations coordinator wants Claude to summarise patient case notes to speed up a backlog. What should the coordinator do first?
options: A) Use a personal account so that the summaries do not appear in the organisation's shared workspace.
B) Ask Claude to confirm that it complies with health privacy rules before pasting the case notes into a chat.
C) Establish whether the organisation permits patient data in the tool, and under which plan and safeguards.
D) Remove the patients' surnames while keeping their dates of birth and record numbers in the notes.
correct_answers: C) Establish whether the organisation permits patient data in the tool, and under which plan and safeguards.
explanations: Moving regulated data to a personal account removes oversight and makes the exposure worse.
Compliance is determined by the organisation's own assessment and agreements, not by asking the tool.
Correct. Regulated health data requires an authorisation and safeguards decision before any of it is entered.
Dates of birth and record numbers still identify people, so this is not meaningful de-identification.
